propositions: A check producing a definite pass/fail result when the producer never ran or emitted nothing cannot distinguish its verdict from its own failure, creating a fail-open oracle antipattern in test code and shipped error-handling code.

The fail-open pattern has a mirror: a check can produce a confident failing result for a reason other than the condition it verifies, such as wrong input or no producer output, causing false alarms as costly as false passes.

Fail-open detection language must be added to the existing tests criterion (test-oracle population) and error-handling criterion (shipped-code population) rather than creating a new criterion, provided calibration replay on nine recorded instances confirms reliable firing from both hosts.

Absence assertions derived from subprocess/file/network output or grepped from another tool's output require established producer liveness checks (exit status, non-empty capture, or asserted presence) to distinguish absence-of-failure from check-failure.

Calibration acceptance requires all nine pre-fix seeded cases to fire with quoted claims naming the fail-open defect, and all nine post-fix cases to yield zero findings, with FP posture recorded against standing no-fire families.

The code-review author guide (rebar explain review) must document the fail-open pattern with at least two worked examples from the calibration corpus, served through src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md.
